General lore:
Kingdom of Disco dates back to the early Roman Empire days when romans settled the area after taking it over from Greece. The land stayed with the Romans until the collapse of the empire when the Byzantines would take over. The Byzantines would also eventually lose the territory after the people rose up against their rule. The Kingdom slayed the Byzantines in the famed battle of Reunion's peak, when the Byzantine forces were defeated by king Discorius. The territory remained independent even from the Ottomans after the king was able to decisively defeat the Ottomans multiple times, keeping the Ottomans away and letting the Kingdom build. The Kingdom become a dominant power in trading rivaling the the Venetians and even fighting them multiple ways. By 1689the kingdom would face its downfall after the battle of Torrential bay was lost to the Venetians, losing the Kingdom major islands it controlled. The Island would remain a neutral power and didn't see more action until WW1, when they assisted the Greeks in kicking the Ottomans out of the Balkans. In 1924, King Zo was crowned king after the late death of his father. Zo was only 16 when crowned but showed well discipline and was well loved by the people. Zo's rule would eventually tighten as the king grew more tyrannical. Zo would essentially lock the country into a dictatorship, changing the constitution to put him in total power. The country was very much split on this, with some seeing the rule as tyrannical and to put the king out of power, while others showed much support for the king. A large opposing party rose up and started actively working against the king. The group was called the ATG and essentially heightened tensions to new extremes. On December 15, 1937 ATG members Nash Donahue and Ebin Hartman sued the King. The case was ultimately lost by the ATG but the news was one of the major events that put the country on the verge of civil war. (edited)

[996704089389932565] hobo_mpik | Wednesday, July 13, 2022 4:06 AM | UTC 2022-07-13T09:06:12.777000+00:00
On June 1st, 1938, the King announced his support with the Nazi government and the Axis after multiple visits with Hitler and Bennito and reportedly went extremely well. The Duo were supposedly great friends and exchanged many gifts.  On July 10th, 1943 King Zo announced that the ATG was herby banned and anyone supporting it were "traitors". Major members and Founders Ebin Hartman and Nash Donahue fled to Lucania, which hosted one of the biggest ATG bases and declared that the ATG must not be stopped and that "If blood is to be spilled for the people, and guns to be raised for change, then the people will fight." The very next day they raised their flags in rebellion and seized the town. The ATG enacted operation "Royal Blood" and began the revolution. by July 11th, 1943 the civil war had begun.

ALTIS BLEEDS INTO STALEMATE
Five Days of Battle Leave Turkish Lodgment Isolated, Greek Counterpressure Rising, Diplomats Moving In

By Elena Virelli, RBD War Desk

ALTIS, AEGEAN — After five days of savage fighting, the battle for Altis has hardened into a brutal localized stalemate, with Turkish troops still holding the airport terminal and immediate perimeter but losing control of the island’s dominant radar ridge after repeated Greek assaults.

The original Turkish operation, launched after Ankara’s strikes on suspected military systems on the island, aimed to seize key points quickly and force a political settlement before the crisis spread. Instead, the fighting has settled into a blood-soaked deadlock.

The radar site itself is now a ruin, destroyed first by Turkish missile strikes and then rendered unusable through Greek demolition. The runway has been cratered and remains out of service, denying either side the ability to convert the airfield into a fixed-wing lifeline.

Air Battle Ends in No Decision

Neither side now controls the skies over Altis. Turkish and Greek aircraft have both suffered losses, and after yesterday’s renewed dogfighting, direct overflight of the island has sharply decreased.

Turkish Foothold Under Severe Pressure

Turkish lead elements, inserted by helicopter in the opening phase of the battle, paid heavily for the assault. Parts of the initial landing force were cut down almost immediately under concentrated defensive fire near the airfield.

Though Turkish troops eventually secured the terminal complex, they were unable to hold the radar ridge. Greek forces, reinforced in the first hours of the crisis, fought their way back onto the high ground and have used mortars and probing attacks to keep the Turkish perimeter under constant pressure.

Greek Recovery, But No Breakthrough

[1493871781394776165] big_zo | Wednesday, April 15, 2026 2:13 AM | UTC 2026-04-15T07:13:07.480000+00:00

Heavier Greek follow-on forces remain largely uncommitted, a sign that Athens may be seeking to avoid the kind of escalation that would drag the wider region into war.

No Mainland Strikes, No Naval Clash

For now, the most important fact remains what has not happened.

There have been:

no strikes on the Greek or Turkish mainland,
no major naval engagement,
no widening of the conflict beyond Altis itself.

That restraint, however reluctant, is the only reason the crisis remains politically containable.

Diplomacy Takes Over as Ammunition Runs Low

Military sources indicate both sides are now suffering severe sustainment problems on the island. Ammunition is running low, medical capacities are strained, and neither side appears capable of achieving a clean battlefield decision without accepting much larger political risks.

At the United Nations, discussions are accelerating around an international commission and ceasefire mechanism, while outside powers push both governments toward a settlement neither will openly admit they now need.

CEASEFIRE FREEZES ALTIS, BUT TURKISH TROOPS REFUSE TO LEAVE AIRPORT
UN Observers Arrive as Buffer Zone Locks In New Aegean Standoff

By Elena Virelli, RBD War Desk

ALTIS, AEGEAN — A fragile ceasefire has taken hold on Altis after days of bloody fighting, but the crisis is far from over. Turkish forces are refusing to leave the airport complex, where they remain dug in under the watch of newly arrived United Nations observers.

A buffer zone has now been established between Turkish and Greek positions, sharply reducing the likelihood of immediate renewed assaults but formalizing what officials privately describe as a highly unstable armed standoff.

Both Turkey and Greece have used the ceasefire window to move food and basic supplies to their forces on the island, a sign that neither side believes the confrontation is truly finished.

Airport Becomes Political Center of the Crisis

Turkish commanders appear to have made a deliberate decision to hold the airport rather than withdraw under pressure. The move preserves a physical Turkish presence on the island, even as broader military ambitions have been checked by the ceasefire and international monitoring.

Greek officials have condemned the continued Turkish presence as an unacceptable occupation of key infrastructure, but Athens has so far stopped short of attempting to break the ceasefire by force.

[1495837262355763200] big_zo | Monday, April 20, 2026 12:23 PM | UTC 2026-04-20T17:23:14.658000+00:00
UN Moves to Freeze, Not Solve

UN personnel are now on the island, tasked with observing compliance, monitoring the buffer zone, and reporting on any violations. Diplomats say the immediate objective is to prevent a return to open combat, not to settle the underlying dispute.

That distinction matters. The shooting may have stopped, but the political struggle over Altis has only entered a new phase.

Both Sides Dig In

Military sources indicate that both armies remain tense, undersupplied compared to peacetime standards, and deeply suspicious of the other’s intentions. The arrival of food and basic supplies has eased immediate pressure, but it has also made clear that both sides are preparing for a prolonged standoff rather than a quick resolution.

No Wider War — For Now

The ceasefire has, at least temporarily, preserved the one fact outside powers cared about most: the conflict remains local.

There have been no mainland strikes, no major naval clashes, and no direct intervention by larger powers. That restraint, however uneasy, is the only reason Altis has not yet become the spark for a much wider crisis.

The Battle Ends, the Dispute Begins

For now, the front lines on Altis have gone quiet.

The argument over who controls the island — and who gets blamed for what happened there — has not.

RBD will continue coverage as the Altis ceasefire enters its first full monitored day.

What is Horizon Dynamics?

Horizon Dynamics is a Reunion-based defense and industrial conglomerate led by Emilio Curro. The company was established through the strategic consolidation and acquisition of several underperforming military-industrial firms during a period of stagnation in Reunion’s defense production sector.
Notably, Horizon Dynamics has integrated multiple aerospace manufacturers into its portfolio, along with the revival of Lucania Motorworks, which has recently resumed production under new management.

What is the goal of Horizon Dynamics?

Horizon Dynamics is committed to reestablishing Reunion as a competitive force in advanced defense manufacturing. The company’s primary objective is the development and production of domestically manufactured aircraft for the Reunion Air Force, while also positioning itself as a supplier to key Western defense markets.
In parallel, Horizon Dynamics aims to address growing demand for high-performance, fuel-efficient military vehicles, with a particular focus on next-generation transport and logistics platforms.

What is Horizon Dynamics currently pursuing?

Horizon Dynamics is presently undergoing a comprehensive restructuring phase while initiating the development of three major operational campuses:
Reunion — Aerospace engineering and advanced aircraft development
Lucania — Vehicle engineering and automotive production
Split — Large-scale manufacturing and industrial fabrication

Following the establishment of these facilities, the company intends to acquire and develop a network of large-scale airfields to support testing, production, and deployment operations. These efforts will culminate in the development of the company’s flagship aerospace platform, the Harpye.

[1117635220036931664] big_zo | Sunday, June 11, 2023 9:03 PM | UTC 2023-06-12T02:03:21.115000+00:00
President Ebin Hartmann - Ebin was born in Steinberg in 1916 to a poor family that made most of their money from their farm. Not too much is known about his childhood besides the fact that he completed High School and was accepted into a University in Italy to continue his studies. By age 19 he had left the University to assist his ailing father in the farm, when he met a man named Nash Donahue who he was friend with in High School. The two shared similar ideas about government, both disliking how much direct power the king held. In 1935 they formed a group named the "Anti-Tyranical-Group" or the ATG. They would actively protest the King from their headquarters in Steinberg until one day, men from the Legio Equestris threatened to arrest members of the ATG in the headquarters. The ATG would refuse and The Legio Equestris began firing on the building, claiming the men inside where shooting back, which they where not. The building caught fire after the Legio Equestris began throwing Molotov's, and nearly 43 people died in the tragedy. Ebin and Nash where visiting Lucania with members of the ATG where they avoided certain death. This massacre caused Ebin and Nash to meet up with another anti-government faction based in Lucania and they spent 2 years gathering equipment via connections into local garrisons. 
"If blood is to be spilled for the people, and guns to be raised for change, then the people will fight." -Ebin Hartmann 
The very next day they raised their flags in rebellion and seized the town. The ATG enacted operation "Royal Blood" and began the revolution. by July 11th, 1943 the civil war had begun.

In 1943, the ATG gathered up and captured a munitions plant in Lucania. This sparked the Disco Civil War which ended in 1947.

Hartmann was pardoned following the ceasefire and went on to live in Reunion, working as a politician and assisting in reconstruction efforts. In 1973 he was eventually elected president following a long presidential campaign (edited)

The unpopularity of the monarchy led to this party going underground. The party grew heavily in popularity following the 1968 Trident Nuclear Facility near meltdown. The Socialist Party of Reunion (Socialist-Leftist) - The Socialist Party takes its roots back to 1926 in Reunion when The Socialist Party of Torrental was formed. The Socialist Party of Torrental was a group of Reunionite Socialists who sought a revolution against the monarchy. The Party went on to join the 1943 Disco Civil War, siding with the Democratic Reunion Party. The Socialists formed The Socialist Party of Reunion in 1956 after going quiet for a few years. The Socialists believe in very common socialist ideas

The Revolutionary front actively believes in Marxist-Leninist communism and pushed for the Civil War. During the 1943 Disco Civil War, The Revolutionary Front supported with thousands of men, spies, weapons manufacturing, and propaganda (However the propaganda was communist in nature and wasn't very effective). The Revolutionary Front leadership where among the few men killed during the trial following the end of the civil war, and the party fell into obscurity until 1974 when the Reunion Senate, which was majority controlled by the Hartmann party, decided to accept bribes from the Revolutionary Front which let them operate freely as long as they paid a fee (Communism was and is still illegal in Reunion). Currently the Revolutionary Front pushes for a second civil war, promoting propaganda making Reunion seem like a racist, class oriented hellscape where only rich Disconians are allowed to suceed, while the poor struggle. The party first ran under the leadership of war hero Chester R. McPeak, who appealed to those of more traditional and the right leaning, despite his more liberal ideals. Chester lead the Conservative party to be that of a moderate party. The Conservative party would form a coalition with the Royalist Party of Reunion to secure a close election against the Hartman Party. Chester would lead for two terms before declaring his sudden retirement from politics. Their sudden drop in popularity was unable to challenge the Hartman party until the Trident Nuclear Scandal and the release of the Trident Papers (See History Channel). 

The Conservative party is a moderate party that prioritizes domestic production, neutrality, and domestic issues relating to the economy.

The party was formed after the civil war ended and was lead by prominent rebel leader Ebin Hartman. Ebin was a skilled politician, author, and lawyer among other things; his leadership skills were keen and the nation saw much needed reform during his three term rule, which passed with relative ease due to his status and the Hartman holding majority rule in the parliament and minor houses. During his third term Hartman and the party would face the Trident Scandal, which would cause Hartman to step down from the presidency before accusations could be thrown at him. Many viewed Hartman as a responsible figure for doing this, others not so much, but the effects would lead to the Hartman party loosing the next year to the Conservatives.

Strangely enough, nothing pointing to where the clones could've gone have shown up and the area had to be put on extensive military watch for the protection of civilians. 
On February 20th one of the clones was found dead in a hunting cabin out in the middle of the forest near the village. The clone was missing its right arm, and was cut open. The following organs were missing: Heart, Stomach, Liver, Small intestine, Frontal lobe of the brain, Gallbladder, and the lift kidney. The clone was reported to have an abnormally large smile with eyes wide open. The team ruled that it could've only been a rouge clone that would've done this. The body was recovered and taken back to Younger Industries while the scene was thoroughly cleaned. 
On February 23rd, another dead clone was found. His body was on the beach and was lying on his stomach. He was missing both of his legs. Near the body spelled a message saying "FJJODM". The team is still unsure of what it means. This clone was even more strange as it was in perfect shape and further examination determined the clone was not suffering from anything when it died. 
 
None of this seems right, what could've happened to these clones?

[1000031022471192607] hobo_mpik | Friday, July 22, 2022 8:26 AM | UTC 2022-07-22T13:26:15.435000+00:00
In repsonse to the loss of Lucania, Order 556 has been activated. All troops south of Lucania and north of Steienberg are to slowly retreat to the Coastal town of Prospect. 
Light's Stockade (The Military camp/Training camp) near Prospect MUST have its equipment evacuated. This equipment is invaluable due to our situation as of now.

[1030736775569756180] big_zo | Saturday, October 15, 2022 1:59 AM | UTC 2022-10-15T06:59:57.459000+00:00
The Julian Squadron has already been established as incredibly brutal in their ways, but one thing about them is not only do they believe in Christian-Pagan values, they also have medals and other memorabilia of Roman gods. Commander [Redacted] (KIA) of the Julian Squadron had his men, during training, learn pagan chants and also reportedly most of the men, before leaving their planes, shouted, "SOL INVICTUS!". Commander [Redacted] (KIA) was killed in action over Lucania, he reportedly was injured upon falling through the roof of a collapsing building and was captured, his location is currently unknown.

[1030741852334334012] big_zo | Saturday, October 15, 2022 2:20 AM | UTC 2022-10-15T07:20:07.854000+00:00
===
The Brigade that landed in Steinberg was the 3rd Julian Brigade which was nearly entirely destroyed except for 25 men, these men where sent home if they requested, the ones who chose to stay where sent to the Reunionists

[1030744800422531093] big_zo | Saturday, October 15, 2022 2:31 AM | UTC 2022-10-15T07:31:50.733000+00:00
===
Documents have been written up to transform the current absolute monarchy into a semi-constitutional-parliamentary-monarchy.

[1136251413236826273] big_zo | Wednesday, August 2, 2023 5:57 AM | UTC 2023-08-02T10:57:27.446000+00:00

[1136643476755337337] big_zo | Thursday, August 3, 2023 7:55 AM | UTC 2023-08-03T12:55:22.673000+00:00

[1136643537203630181] big_zo | Thursday, August 3, 2023 7:55 AM | UTC 2023-08-03T12:55:37.085000+00:00

Reunion lost 97 men during the counter attack

[1142599540566921299] big_zo | Saturday, August 19, 2023 6:22 PM | UTC 2023-08-19T23:22:38.944000+00:00

[1142628552085348352] big_zo | Saturday, August 19, 2023 8:17 PM | UTC 2023-08-20T01:17:55.829000+00:00

[1147763475251200100] big_zo | Sunday, September 3, 2023 12:22 AM | UTC 2023-09-03T05:22:16.914000+00:00

[1148369274163970080] big_zo | Monday, September 4, 2023 4:29 PM | UTC 2023-09-04T21:29:30.630000+00:00

[1227136887534387233] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 1:03 AM | UTC 2024-04-09T06:03:53.089000+00:00
Croatia launched a large counter offensive on March 1st, 1991, the offensive resulted in massive casualties for Croatia, losing approximately 540 men, while inflicting only 320 casualties on Reunion. Croatia also lost many medium tanks while only taking out a handful of Reunion light tanks. Reunions worst losses however comes from the 3 CAS bombers that where shot down (edited)

[1227138104930861066] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 1:08 AM | UTC 2024-04-09T06:08:43.339000+00:00
The Reunionists countered with heavy artillery forcing the Croatians to retreat down to Seget Vranjica along the west coast, and the small village of Stanici on the East coast

[1227138422284619827] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 1:09 AM | UTC 2024-04-09T06:09:59.002000+00:00
Croatians pulled back into the mountains just north of Split, leaving debris in the road including chopped down trees, empty crates, and even mines

[1227160333404344320] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 2:37 AM | UTC 2024-04-09T07:37:03.020000+00:00
The Reunionists began to push inland, taking the town of Dugopolje. Reunion killed 289 Croats, losing only 167 men. The Reunionists lost 2 apcs and a light tank in the fighting but managed to take out many modern Croatian APC's

[1227161448162005012] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 2:41 AM | UTC 2024-04-09T07:41:28.799000+00:00
The Reunionists also managed to capture and repair a Croatian recon APC

[1227162201006276658] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 2:44 AM | UTC 2024-04-09T07:44:28.291000+00:00
Between early March to mid April the Croatians lost nearly 1.3K men to coastal bombardments, causing them to retreat from much of the Dalmatian coast inland. The croats resort to blowing bridges along the coast and mining important roads inland as they retreat

[1227478267305398402] big_zo | Tuesday, April 9, 2024 11:40 PM | UTC 2024-04-10T04:40:24.369000+00:00
Reunion continues with their operations, drafted up by General Donahue, to take the supply hub of Knin. The fighting inland heated up mid March and by March 22nd, Reunion casualties where nearing the 500 mark while Croatia was in the 550's to 600's

[1227497602724139069] big_zo | Wednesday, April 10, 2024 12:57 AM | UTC 2024-04-10T05:57:14.292000+00:00
The city just outside of Knin was taken, losing Reunion nearly 927 and Croatia only 798 men. Reunion suffered light tank casualties and lost only one helicopter during the operation. The Croatians did not have enough time to retreat most of their supplies, crippling much of their long term fighting capabilities in the region. This forced the Croats to pull back a decent ways to their nearby supply hub of Zadar, Croatian high command chose to abandon much of Dalmatia as they couldnt afford to fight in the region. (edited)

[1227499287395438592] big_zo | Wednesday, April 10, 2024 1:03 AM | UTC 2024-04-10T06:03:55.949000+00:00
The Serbian army begins a large assault through Bosnian territory (Still under yugoslavia until 92'), the move cuts off Croatian troops, this forces them into a siege by Yugoslavian forces as of April 16th, 1991

[1228186429419683970] big_zo | Thursday, April 11, 2024 10:34 PM | UTC 2024-04-12T03:34:23.374000+00:00
On April 29th, 1991, 2,500 Marines landed on Zadar, taking the city within a few hours thanks to heavy naval gun support from the Reunion navy. The marines are pushing out towards a bridge to set up defences as the army comes in to take their spot. Croatia was able to take down one of our apaches with a well placed shot from a t-57 which was quickly dispached (edited)

[1228207244710252645] big_zo | Thursday, April 11, 2024 11:57 PM | UTC 2024-04-12T04:57:06.126000+00:00
The Supply hub of Knin was taken after brutal fighting for a castle that the Croatians turned into a fort. Reunionists lost 313 men while Croatia lost over 1200 men. The loss of Knin has caused the Croatian army in Dalmatia to go into a frenzied retreat north, following heavy Serbian attacks due to the crippled logistics

[1] SITREP / BATTLE REPORT / CASUALTY REPORT
[2] TURKISH ARMED FORCES – OPERATION KALKAN-93
[3] As of 04:30 Local, 11 October 1993 (Day 5 – Early Morning)
[4] From: Kalkan-6A (New Second-in-Command, acting Company Commander)
[5] To: All Elements / Higher Command
[6] 1. SITUATION SUMMARY
[7] The island remains in a tense, localized standoff. Turkish forces hold the airfield terminal and immediate perimeter but have been driven off the radar ridge. The radar installation is completely destroyed (initial Tomahawk strike + Greek engineer demolition). The airfield runway is cratered and unusable for fixed-wing operations. No air superiority exists for either side following yesterday’s dogfight.
[8] Greek forces have established positions around the island and are actively probing our remaining lodgment. Their QRF (G2) is fully committed and has received no further reinforcement due to the mutual escalation standoff. Greek Follow-on (G3) remains at full strength but has not yet committed in force.
[9] No resupply has reached either side since the initial insertion. Ammunition, medical supplies, and food are critically low across all Turkish units.
[10] 2. BATTLE REPORT (Chronological)
[11] 06 Oct, 20:00 – Insertion: Heliborne assault begins. Alpha Platoon suffers catastrophic losses during a misplaced landing at the airfield. Two full squads are wiped out in the opening minutes by concentrated Greek security fire.
[12] 07 Oct, ~04:00: Airport terminal and immediate perimeter secured despite heavy casualties. Company Commander lands at first light and assumes command.
[13] 07–08 Oct: Forces dig in and consolidate. Plans for rapid reinforcement are placed on hold due to mutual threats of escalation. Greek QRF (G2) arrives by boat at ~01:30 on 07 Oct (1.5 hours post-touchdown) but receives no additional support.
[14] 09 Oct (Day 3): Three Greek squads supported by a BTR-40 and four mortars launch a determined assault on the radar ridge. After a 5-hour gunfight, Turkish forces are driven off the hill. Two heroic soldiers from Bravo Platoon remain in their sandbag positions, delaying the Greeks long enough for survivors to link up with the road defense squad. Both men are killed in place.
[15] Night of 09–10 Oct (Night 3): Greek forces (~80 troops) launch a heavy night assault on the airport terminal, supported by BTR-40, mortar fire, and the BMP-1. Company Commander is killed by an RPG detonation while personally defending the terminal. New Second-in-Command assumes command. BMP-1 is destroyed by a TOW/rocket hit at close range while attempting to withdraw at first light.
[16] 10 Oct: Greek aircraft attempt to regain air superiority. Dogfight results in Turkey losing 2 F-16s and Greece losing 1 Su-27. Both sides withdraw from direct overflight of the island. Airfield is further cratered by Greek close air support.
[17] Night of 10–11 Oct: Renewed heavy Greek assault on the airport perimeter (nearly 80 troops, BTR, and mortar support). Alpha Platoon is cut down severely and loses most forward positions by morning. Bravo Platoon is currently tasked with eliminating the Greek mortar position on the ridge but reports extremely low ammunition.
[18] The fight has remained strictly localized to the island as per High Command orders. No naval or mainland strikes have occurred.
[19] 3. CASUALTY REPORT (as of 04:30, 11 Oct)
[20] Turkish Forces (Lead Package only)
[21] Company HQ Element: 10 → Effective 4 (2 KIA, 4 WIA)
[22] Alpha Platoon: 50 → Effective 20 (16 KIA, 14 WIA) – Two squads completely wiped out during initial landing.
[23] Bravo Platoon: 45 → Effective 12 (17 KIA, 1 WIA, 15 MIA) – Heavy losses on radar ridge; two men held final positions to the death.
[24] Charlie Platoon: 55 → Effective 35 (6 KIA, 14 WIA)
[25] Total Turkish Effective Strength: 61 out of original 160 (≈44% casualties).
[26] Greek Forces
[27] Latent Skeleton: 120 → Effective 0 (42 KIA, 34 WIA, 44 MIA)
[28] QRF (G2): 220 → Effective 124 (96 KIA)
[29] Follow-on (G3): 650 → Effective 650 (no major contact yet)
[30] Greek Vehicles Status:
[31] BMP-1: Destroyed
[32] BTR-40: Destroyed / out of action
[33] GAZ-66 Trucks: 2 operational
[34] DShK (mounted): 7 operational
[35] NSV: 4 operational
[36] SPG-9: 2 operational
[37] Mortars (60/82mm): 4 operational (still active and firing)
[38] 4. LOGISTICS / MUNITIONS / SUSTAINMENT STATUS (04:30, 11 Oct)
[39] No resupply has reached Turkish forces since the initial heliborne insertion. All consumption is based on four days of near-continuous fighting, multiple mortar barrages, and heavy defensive actions.
[40] Turkish Remaining (Lead Package only)
[41] Small Arms Ammo: Extremely low – less than 1 crate remaining across the entire company.
[42] Heavy Weapons Ammo: Critical – < 0.5 crates (MG3 and TOW rounds nearly exhausted). Bravo Platoon reports they can sustain current mortar-hunting mission for only 1–2 more hours.
[43] Explosives/Demo: ~0.5 crate left.
[44] Medical Supplies: Critical – < 1 box remaining. CCP is overwhelmed; many WIA cannot receive proper treatment.
[45] Food / Water: Very low – < 1 box remaining. Troops have been on half-rations for 48+ hours.
[46] Fuel: 400 liters left
[47] Repair Parts: Exhausted – 0 sets remaining.
[48] Fortify Budget: Spent – < 30 points left (most positions are now sandbag-and-wire only).
[49] Greek QRF Logistics Estimate (your best assessment as Zeus)
[50] Also critically low on small arms and mortar rounds after four days of fighting and no resupply.
[51] They still possess the four mortars and heavy MGs (DShK/NSV) but are conserving ammunition for the next major push on the airport.
[52] Overall Assessment
[53] We are in a critically depleted state. The lodgment is holding by a thread at the airfield terminal only. Bravo Platoon’s current mission to silence the Greek mortars is vital but high-risk due to ammunition constraints. The new Second-in-Command recommends immediate prioritization of any possible emergency resupply drop or extraction of wounded if the standoff allows.
[54] End of report.
[55] Kalkan-6A
[56] Acting Company Commander

[1] CONFIDENTIAL — EYES ONLY
 Via secure diplomatic channel
 From: Office of the President of Serbia
 To: President Dax Donahue II, Republic of Reunion
 Subject: Betrayal of Confidence — Bosnian Arms Scheme / Ploče Fallout
[2] President Donahue,
[3] I am writing in anger and in disbelief.
[4] Serbia has treated Reunion as a partner of consequence—one capable of discipline, statecraft, and keeping its own house in order. What we have learned in the last forty-eight hours makes that assumption look naïve.
[5] We now have credible intelligence indicating that your chief financial adviser was working with Bosnian actors, and that multiple figures of power in Reunion—not low-level smugglers, not “unauthorized patriots”—were engaged in a plan to arm Bosnia through covert channels. The structure of the plan is too detailed, too resourced, and too coordinated to be dismissed as rumor. There are names. There are routes. There are intermediaries. There are financial movements that do not occur by accident.
[6] Let me be clear: if Serbia is being used as a convenient friend to keep your state upright while elements inside your system play both sides—then you are gambling with a relationship you cannot afford to lose.
[7] What makes this worse is the timing and context. We were preparing our own arrangement with Bosnia—one based on hard realities, not sentiment. Bosnia abruptly backed out for reasons still unknown, and now the outline becomes visible: a full scheme laid out to move weapons, money, and equipment, with Reunion-linked actors in the picture. That is not “policy drift.” That is betrayal.
[8] You will understand why I am alarmed by what remains unknown. If the deeper relationship between Reunion power-brokers and Bosnian factions were to become public, it would suggest something far more corrosive: that powerful Reunionists were willing to tolerate—perhaps even enable—events like Ploče for their own purposes. I do not need you to confirm that for me in writing. I am telling you that Serbia will not be pulled into a fog where we end up carrying the blame for other people’s games.
[9] Here is what I require, immediately:
[10] A direct secure call within 12 hours with you personally—not an aide, not a minister—so I can hear plainly whether your government is in control of itself.
[11] Immediate suspension and isolation (administrative leave, access revoked, communications restricted) of any financial, intelligence, or logistics officials credibly named in this scheme—pending investigation.
[12] A written assurance, transmitted through official channels, that Reunion will not facilitate arms transfers to Bosnia through criminal syndicates, cut-outs, or state-connected “private” structures.

[3] Civilians evacuated first, daylight if possible, with UN witnessing that no one is “disappeared” mid-corridor.

[1] Industrial Air Capability & Dual-Use Acceleration Act (1992)
[3] Section 1 — Short Title
[4] This Act may be cited as the Industrial Air Capability & Dual-Use Acceleration Act (1992).
[6] Section 2 — Findings & Strategic Purpose
[7] Parliament finds:
[8] Reunion’s current air force modernization depends heavily on foreign platforms and sustainment chains.
[9] Supply vulnerability poses a direct risk to readiness and sovereignty.
[10] Domestic aerospace capability reduces long-term defense costs and strengthens export potential.
[11] Existing defense appropriations include unexecuted or delayed procurement authority that can be repurposed without reducing near-term operational readiness.
[12] Purpose:
[13] Establish a domestic aerospace industrial base
[14] Reduce long-term procurement costs
[15] Support maintenance, training, and future aircraft development
[17] Section 3 — Funding Authorization
[18] Authorizes up to $6.0B USD equivalent over FY1993–FY1995.
[19] Funding Sources:
[20] Reallocation of unexecuted defense procurement funds (primary source)
[21] Up to $1.0B from contingency reserve only upon joint certification by:
[22] Minister of Finance
[23] Minister of Defense
[24] No new deficit authority is created beyond existing approved borrowing limits.
[26] Section 4 — National Aerospace Capability Program (NACP)
[27] Establishes the National Aerospace Capability Program under joint authority of:
[28] Ministry of Finance
[29] Ministry of Defense
[30] Ministry of Technology & Communications
[31] Mandate:
[32] Develop domestic capacity in:
[33] Airframe manufacturing
[34] Avionics integration
[35] Maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO)
[36] Pilot and technical training systems
[37] Prioritize dual-use technologies applicable to both civilian and military aviation.
[39] Section 5 — Industrial Partner Designation
[40] The government may designate one or more prime industrial partners to execute program objectives.
[41] Selection criteria:
[42] Demonstrated industrial capability
[43] Existing defense or advanced manufacturing experience
[44] Ability to scale production within 24–36 months
[45] Compliance with national security and FMS requirements
[46] Designated partners may receive:
[47] Capital investment contracts
[48] Development grants
[49] Long-term procurement agreements
[50] (This is where Horizon Dynamics realistically becomes the primary recipient without naming it directly.)
[52] Section 6 — Defense Reprogramming Authority
[53] The Ministry of Defense is authorized to reprogram delayed or non-critical procurement funds into NACP projects.
[54] Conditions:
[55] Must not degrade current readiness below defined thresholds
[56] Must not interfere with:
[57] Active deployments
[58] Critical modernization deliveries (F-16, radar, air defense)
[59] Reporting:
[60] Quarterly disclosure to Parliamentary Defense Committee
[61] Certification of readiness impact
[63] Section 7 — Technology Development & Aircraft Pathway
[64] NACP shall fund:
[65] Prototype development for domestic aircraft platforms
[66] Licensed production or adaptation of existing designs where feasible
[67] Component-level independence (engines excluded initially unless viable)
[68] Priority timeline:
[69] 0–2 years: MRO + training infrastructure
[70] 2–5 years: Licensed assembly / partial domestic production
[71] 5+ years: Indigenous aircraft design capability
[73] Section 8 — Financial Controls & Oversight
[74] Independent audit authority established under Ministry of Finance.
[75] Safeguards:
[76] Spending tied to milestone completion
[77] Contract clawback provisions for non-performance
[78] Foreign technology compliance audits (US/French requirements)
[79] Annual review submitted to:
[80] President
[81] Parliament
[82] Defense Council
[84] Section 9 — Economic Impact Mandate
[85] Program must:
[86] Generate domestic employment
[87] Increase industrial output
[88] Reduce long-term defense import dependency
[89] Secondary objective:
[90] Establish export-capable aerospace sector within 10 years

sources.text:
[1] Reunion Broadcasting Daily Network (RBD)
 Evening News Reel — 16 October 1992
 Broadcast Time: 19:00 | Reunion City Studio
[3] [OPENING STING — brass, drums, fast montage: ports, parliament, offshore rigs, soldiers marching, currency tickers]
[4] ANCHOR (Studio):
 Good evening. This is RBD. Tonight: a fragile peace settles over the Dalmatian coast as the new demarcation line takes hold—while at home, the economy strains under emergency spending, war disruption, and market fear. But offshore, a survey result has set off what some lawmakers are calling the first credible “exit ramp” from crisis: Reunion’s newly confirmed light-oil deposits.
[5] And in Parliament: the birth of two new giants—one in oil, one in defense industry—reshaping the nation’s economic future in real time.
[7] Segment 1 — Dalmatian Peace Deal Holds… For Now
[8] [ROLL VIDEO: map graphic of Dalmatian coast; Zadar highlighted down to just north of Šibenik]
[9] ANCHOR:
 One month after the ceasefire collapsed into renewed combat, Reunion and Croatia signed a Croatian-drafted peace instrument on the date the ceasefire ended—locking in a new line of control and a 12-year “non-war” clause.
[10] Under the deal: Croatia assumes administration of Zadar southward to a line just north of Šibenik, and Reunion forces are permitted to withdraw under safe-passage provisions, including explicit language requiring Croatian forces not to be fired upon during withdrawal.
[11] But analysts inside the Assembly are warning the text is deliberately brittle—its breach clauses broad enough that “any little thing can break it,” as one senior committee member put it today.
[12] [CUT TO: Parliament hallway scrum]
[13] RBD PARLIAMENT CORRESPONDENT:
 The governing blocs are publicly calling this “a pause to rebuild,” but privately, MPs describe it as a treaty written with tripwires. The RRP’s moderates are pushing for strict compliance protocols and incident reporting to avoid accidental breach. The NSF calls it “temporary paper,” while the RCA claims it prevents outright collapse of the front and buys time.
[15] Segment 2 — Economy: A Confidence Crisis, Not Just a Budget Crisis
[16] [ROLL GRAPHIC: GDP in RMC and USD equivalent; “2.9T RMC → ~2.4T RMC”]
[17] ANCHOR:
 Reunion’s economy has taken a sharp hit since the start of Donahue’s term. Treasury estimates now place GDP around 2.4 trillion RMC, down from 2.9 trillion RMC—a decline that roughly corresponds to a fall from ~$500 billion to ~$414 billion at the current conversion rate of 5.8 RMC to $1.
[18] Finance officials emphasize the drop is being driven by a cascade:
[19] war disruption and shipping insurance risk,
[20] business closures and tightening credit,
[21] softening tax collections as trade slows and firms delay payments,
[22] and confidence damage—with households hoarding and markets demanding higher risk premiums.
[23] [ROLL B-ROLL: shuttered storefronts, people lining up at banks, port cranes idle]
[24] RBD ECONOMICS DESK:
 Even as the government raises ministry budgets and accelerates spending commitments—ports, rail, veterans support, food stabilization—revenue reliability is worsening. Analysts stress: this isn’t only about “how much is spent,” but whether the state can keep ports functioning, keep fuel and parts moving, and prevent further shocks to credibility.
[26] Segment 3 — Offshore Oil: Parliament Moves Fast on “80/20”
[27] [ROLL VIDEO: offshore survey ship, sonar screens, then a map of the basin]
[28] ANCHOR:
 The biggest story driving market speculation this week: the newly confirmed offshore light-oil deposits. Parliament has moved quickly to codify the political line: 80% remains nationalized, 20% is privatized by production entitlement, and all private operators must comply with Reunion’s strategic export policy—selling only to approved markets.
[29] The legislation includes:
[30] a domestic supply obligation,
[31] hard-currency signature bonuses paid into a ring-fenced stabilization account,
[32] and security vetting of foreign technical staff.
[33] RBD ENERGY CORRESPONDENT:
 The mood in the Assembly is “drill, but with chains on it.” Everyone wants the solvency narrative, but no one wants to be seen handing sovereignty to foreign majors. Committees have also flagged the diplomatic complication: a significant portion of the deposits sits in waters between Reunion and Greece and within Greek waters—meaning long-term development will require unitization or joint development arrangements.
[35] Segment 4 — Who’s Bidding: Shell, Exxon, France—And the Domestic Bloc
[36] [ROLL GRAPHIC: “Privatized 20% divided into tranches; winners pending/announced in principle”]
[37] ANCHOR:
 Lobbying has surged. Major international bidders have appeared in Reunion City in force—Shell and Exxon leading the charge, with French bidders also pressing offers packaged with training and downstream support. Parliamentary sources say the goal is to split awards to avoid dependence on any single foreign operator.
[38] Domestic plays
[39] Younger Industries has mounted the largest private domestic bid, framing itself as “the national industrial partner.”
[40] Royla, the new oil arm of the Crown’s expanding holdings network, has secured a stake roughly equivalent to 2% of Reunion’s total oil entitlement—a smaller slice than some expected, but enough to secure board influence and long-term cashflow.
[41] Other domestic industrial groups are positioning for service contracts: rigs, supply vessels, depot operations, and refining logistics.
[42] RBD BUSINESS DESK:
 The risk now is political: oil can stabilize the currency in expectation, but expectations collapse if Parliament fractures over corruption fears—or if export control and revenue ring-fencing are seen as unenforced.
[44] Segment 5 — Horizon Dynamics: One Company to Build the Next Era of War Industry
[45] [ROLL VIDEO: factory floors, truck chassis, radar arrays, machinists in Steinberg and Lucania]
[46] ANCHOR:
 In another major move, Parliament has authorized a consolidation of surviving defense-industrial firms into a single national champion: Horizon Dynamics.
[47] According to committee briefings, Horizon has already begun absorbing:
[48] Lucania Motor Works (heavy vehicle assembly),
[49] Steinberg Ordnance & Foundry (machining and castings),
[50] Reunion Avionics & Instruments Group (electronics and sensors),
[51] Torrental Heavy Logistics Works (trailers, cranes, port equipment),
[52] and a small systems integration bureau now rebranded as Horizon’s R&D spine.
[53] The stated priorities, per Parliamentary committee summaries:
[54] Heavy logistics trucks emphasizing power and reliability over comfort
[55] Radar investment focused first on domestic coastal and ground surveillance
[56] Modern electronics capacity to reduce dependence on imports
[57] Early-stage air power R&D framed as a “long program,” not an immediate replacement fleet
[58] RBD DEFENSE-INDUSTRY CORRESPONDENT:
 There is broad support for the truck program because it directly feeds logistics in both peacetime and crisis. Radar and electronics are seen as slow-burn sovereignty projects. The aviation ambition is the most controversial—committees are insisting on compliance controls and realistic timelines to avoid a prestige sink.
[60] Segment 6 — Royla and the Crown’s New Holdings Structure
[61] [ROLL GRAPHIC: “Royla Holdings” / “Royla Oil” / minority stakes in logistics and security services]
[62] ANCHOR:
 And now to Royla Holdings, the Crown-aligned investment structure that now owns Royla Oil and a growing web of strategic minority positions—ports logistics, supply services, and energy-adjacent contracts. Royalist MPs call it “national capital mobilization.” Critics call it “a parallel state economy.”
[63] In Parliament, the debate is not whether Royla exists—its existence is now fact. The fight is over:
[64] procurement firewalls,
[65] beneficial ownership disclosures,
[66] and whether the new national champions serve the republic—or slowly bend it.
[68] Segment 7 — The National Mood
[69] [ROLL B-ROLL: a market, a recruiting line, a train yard, a quiet church, a closed factory gate]
[70] ANCHOR:
 Public sentiment remains strained: war fatigue, fear of renewed fighting, and deep anxiety about jobs and prices. But oil has changed something subtle: for the first time in weeks, even hardened opposition MPs have stopped saying “we’re finished” and started saying “we might have a way out.”
[71] The question now is whether Parliament can keep unity long enough to turn that prospect into reality.
[73] Bosnia Seeks Foreign Backing; UN Inquiry into Ploče Proposed
[74] ANCHOR:
 RBD has learned that Bosnia’s new leadership has approached both the United States and Saudi Arabia in separate channels requesting peacekeepers and emergency support, as tensions continue to rise across the region.
[75] A senior diplomatic source confirms that the United States has offered to push for a United Nations investigation into the Ploče incident, signaling growing international attention on the confrontation surrounding the port city and the competing accounts of what occurred there.
[76] At the same time, Bosnia has announced that Iraq, Syria, and Libya have jointly delivered what Bosnia describes as two billion dollars’ worth of weapons and military equipment. Bosnian officials claim the shipments are intended to strengthen Bosnia’s ability to fight Reunion, framing the conflict as a defensive struggle and using religious language—calling it a “jihad” and accusing Reunion of aggression.
[77] Reunion officials have not issued a full formal response to the claims of foreign arms deliveries, but parliamentary security figures have already called for urgent briefings on border interdiction and port defenses.
[79] Zo and Curro’s Asia Trip: Beijing Meetings and Investment Diplomacy
[80] ANCHOR:
 In a separate development, Palace sources and economic ministry officials confirm that King Zo III and Finance Minister Emilio Curro have returned from a high-profile diplomatic and business trip through Asia.
[81] The delegation spent roughly a week in Beijing, where they were seen meeting with senior Chinese officials and attending cultural events as part of what was described as a “strategic economic and cultural exchange.” RBD can confirm that one of the most prominent contacts during the visit included a meeting with Jiang Zemin, China’s top leader.
[82] During the Beijing leg, the Palace also confirmed that a stake in the Crown-linked energy venture Royla was sold to Chinese businessman Shao Luxian, a long-standing contact of both Zo and Curro. While exact contract terms were not released, sources describe the sale as bringing in several billion U.S. dollars and positioning Royla as a better-capitalized participant in Reunion’s emerging offshore oil program.
[83] Following Beijing, Zo and Curro continued their trip with stops in Japan and South Korea, meeting business and industrial figures, with discussions reportedly focused on port logistics, industrial tooling, electronics, and long-term investment relationships. On the return journey, they made a brief stop in Saudi Arabia, where Palace sources say they held meetings with members of the royal family regarding economic ties and regional stability.
[85] ANCHOR (Studio):
 These developments come as Parliament faces mounting pressure to address economic anxiety at home while navigating growing international scrutiny abroad. RBD will continue to provide verified updates as official statements and diplomatic moves become public.

[1] FINAL PAPER — SOVEREIGN STABILIZATION TERM LOAN AGREEMENT
[2] (United States – Republic of Reunion)
 Date: September __, 1992 (effective upon satisfaction of Conditions Precedent)
[3] 1. Parties
[4] The United States of America, acting through the U.S. Department of the Treasury (“Lender”).
[5] The Republic of Reunion, acting through the Ministry of Finance and with acknowledgment by the Reunion Central Bank (“Borrower”).
[6] 2. Purpose and Permitted Uses
[7] 2.1 Facility Purpose
[8] This facility is a stabilization and reconstruction loan intended to support:
[9] (a) critical infrastructure repair (power, ports, rail infrastructure, water/sewage, roads, logistics nodes);
[10] (b) medical and veteran services;
[11] (c) civil defense sustainment (maintenance, spare parts, communications, protective/defensive logistics); and Military spending
[12] (d) procurement of rebuilding equipment and technical services under monitored, competitive processes.
[13] 2.2 Prohibited Uses (Absolute)
[14] No proceeds may be used directly or indirectly for:
[15] (i) covert procurement pipelines, arms trafficking, smuggling, or third-party arming;
[16] (ii) financing or expanding militias outside formal state command;
[17] (iii) off-budget security spending or any expenditure not recorded within the Borrower’s audited public accounts;
[18] (iv) payments to any sanctioned/blacklisted entity designated by the Lender.
[19] Breach of Section 2.2 is an Event of Default.
[20] 3. Principal, Currency, and Exchange Convention
[21] 3.1 Principal
[22] USD 90,000,000 (“Principal”).
[23] 3.2 RMC Reference (Borrower’s stated rate)
[24] For reporting purposes only, using the Borrower’s stated convention: $1 USD = 5.8 RMC.
 Principal reference: 522,000,000 RMC.
[25] All payments are due in USD.
[26] 4. Fees and Costs
[27] 4.1 Upfront Facility and Monitoring Fee
[28] 3.0% of Principal due at closing:
[29] USD 2,700,000 (reference: 15,660,000 RMC).
[30] 4.2 Borrower Costs
[31] Borrower bears reasonable costs of monitoring, audit support, and verification travel under this Agreement.
[32] 5. Interest
[33] 5.1 Rate
[34] 12.00% fixed per annum on outstanding principal.
[35] 5.2 Default Interest
[36] Upon an Event of Default, interest increases by +2.00% (to 14.00%) on all overdue amounts until cured and paid.
[37] 6. Tenor, Structure, and Repayment
[38] 6.1 Tenor
[39] 10 years from Closing Date (“Maturity Date”).
[40] 6.2 Repayment Structure
[41] Year 1: interest-only
[42] Years 2–10: nine (9) equal annual payments of principal + interest
[43] 6.3 Payment Schedule (Amounts)
[44] All figures rounded to the nearest dollar.
[45] Year 1 (Interest-Only):
[46] USD 10,800,000 (ref: 62,640,000 RMC)
[47] Years 2–10 (Equal Annual Payments):
[48] USD 16,891,100 per year (ref: 97,968,380 RMC per year)
[49] 6.4 Total Amounts (Illustrative)
[50] Total repaid (principal + interest): USD 162,819,900 (ref: 944,355,419 RMC)
[51] Total including fee (Section 4.1): USD 165,519,900 (ref: 960,015,419 RMC)
[52] 7. Disbursement (Tranches) — “Leash” Mechanics
[53] 7.1 Tranche Plan
[54] Principal is disbursed as follows, subject to conditions:
[55] Tranche A: USD 30,000,000 at Closing
[56] Tranches B–G: USD 10,000,000 each, quarterly over the next 18 months (6 tranches total)
[57] 7.2 Conditions for Each Tranche
[58] Each tranche after Closing requires:
[59] (a) submission and acceptance of audited expenditure statements for prior tranches;
[60] (b) verification that spending complied with Section 2 (Permitted Uses);
[61] (c) continued acceptance and access for the monitoring mission (Section 9);
[62] (d) no uncured Event of Default.
[63] 7.3 Suspension
[64] Lender may suspend or cancel undisbursed tranches if:
[65] any prohibited use is suspected with credible evidence pending review, or
[66] monitoring access is obstructed, or
[67] the Borrower fails reporting deadlines by more than 30 days.
[68] 8. “Lockbox” Debt Service Covenant (Security Without Collateral)
[69] 8.1 Dedicated Debt Service Account
[70] Borrower shall establish a dedicated Debt Service Account held at a mutually agreed correspondent bank (“Lockbox”).
[71] 8.2 Monthly Funding Requirement
[72] Borrower shall fund the Lockbox monthly with an amount sufficient to cover the next scheduled payment with a 90-day buffer, sourced from customs and port receipts and/or other agreed sovereign revenue streams.
[73] 8.3 Trigger
[74] If the Lockbox falls below the required buffer for 30 consecutive days, the Lender may:
[75] suspend tranches, and/or
[76] require additional controls on revenue routing until restored.
[77] 9. Oversight, Monitoring, and Procurement Controls
[78] 9.1 Monitoring Mission
[79] Borrower accepts a U.S. Treasury Monitoring Mission with access to:
[80] contracts, invoices, tender files, delivery confirmations, and recipient ministries;
[81] site visits for major infrastructure purchases;
[82] interviews with procurement officials and auditors.
[83] 9.2 Procurement Rules
[84] For any contract ≥ USD 250,000, Borrower shall:
[85] use competitive tendering unless emergency-waived in writing with justification;
[86] record awards in the national procurement registry;
[87] retain full documentation for inspection.
[88] 9.3 Reporting
[89] Borrower provides quarterly reports including:
[90] tranche spending ledger;
[91] project status and milestones;
[92] variance explanations;
[93] macro indicators (inflation, FX reserves, deficit).
[94] 10. Governance and Conduct Covenants (Non-Financial)
[95] Borrower covenants that during the term:
[96] (a) Borrower will maintain enforceable detention and evidence-handling rules previously accepted publicly;
[97] (b) Borrower will not materially obstruct international monitoring arrangements it has agreed to;
[98] (c) Borrower will maintain central bank operational reporting discipline consistent with its monetary stability framework;
[99] (d) Borrower will not route loan proceeds through any unofficial security structures.
[100] 11. Events of Default
[101] Each of the following constitutes an Event of Default:
[102] Non-payment of any amount due (with a 10-day cure for technical failure).
[103] Any breach of Prohibited Uses (Section 2.2).
[104] Material misrepresentation in any report or certification.
[105] Obstruction/expulsion of the Monitoring Mission (Section 9).
[106] Unlawful diversion of proceeds or refusal to provide documentation.
[107] Cross-default to other external sovereign debt above an agreed threshold.
[108] 12. Remedies
[109] Upon an Event of Default, Lender may:
[110] suspend/cancel undisbursed tranches;
[111] apply default interest (Section 5.2);
[112] accelerate repayment (declare amounts immediately due);
[113] require enhanced controls over the Lockbox routing.
[114] 13. Optional Rate Step-Down (Only After Performance)
[115] 13.1 Step-Down Eligibility
[116] After 18 consecutive months of full compliance (clean audits, no prohibited use, full monitoring access), Lender may reduce the rate on the remaining balance to 10.50% fixed effective at the next anniversary.
[117] 13.2 No Entitlement
[118] This is discretionary. Any compliance breach voids eligibility.
[119] 14. Governing Law and Venue
[120] Governing law: New York law (commercial terms), with disputes subject to jurisdiction in U.S. federal courts as designated by the Lender, and waiver of sovereign immunity to the extent customary for sovereign borrowing instruments.
[121] 15. Entire Agreement
[122] This document and its schedules constitute the entire agreement, superseding prior discussions.
[124] Annex A — GDP Burden (Reunion)
[125] You gave: GDP = 18–20 billion RMC, and $1 = 5.8 RMC, so GDP in USD is roughly $3.10B–$3.45B.
[126] Principal as % of GDP
[127] 522,000,000 RMC / 18,000,000,000 RMC = 2.90%
[128] 522,000,000 RMC / 20,000,000,000 RMC = 2.61%
[129] So the loan is ~2.6%–2.9% of GDP.
[130] Annual debt service as % of GDP (10-year option)
[131] Year 1 interest: 62.64M RMC
[132] 0.348% of GDP (if 18B) to 0.313% (if 20B)
[133] Years 2–10 payment: 97.97M RMC
[134] 0.544% of GDP (if 18B) to 0.490% (if 20B)
[136] Signed

George H. W Bush
[138] Dax Donahue II

sources.path: REUNION/ “Horizon Dynamics”_.docx
sources.text:
[1] Here’s how everyone else reacts in early October 1992 when Strevo drops the “Horizon Dynamics” consolidation bomb and the Crown piles in.
[2] 1) Parliament’s immediate posture
[3] RRP (centrist institutionalists)
[4] Not opposed, but they refuse to rubber-stamp a “royal + Curro megacorp” during a credibility crisis.
[5] They push for hard guardrails: procurement transparency, audited capitalization, conflict-of-interest walls, and export controls consistent with state policy.
[6] RCA (royalists)
[7] All-in, loudly. They frame it as “national revival” and “sovereignty through industry.”
[8] They want Royla and Crown-linked suppliers in the ecosystem (steel, ports, security).
[9] NSF (security-nationalists)
[10] All-in, but with strings: security vetting, closed committees, and “strategic secrecy” exemptions.
[11] They push for Horizon to become the backbone of a permanent mobilization economy.
[12] LUP (labor/left)
[13] Split:
[14] pro-jobs wing supports consolidation if it means domestic employment, worker protections, and civilian tech spillovers.
[15] civil-liberties wing treats it as a “royal-industrial coup by balance sheet” and demands oversight and limits.
[16] Dalmatian lists/minors
[17] Mostly transactional: they want guarantees that Horizon’s truck/logistics production benefits Dalmatia supply chains, not just the core islands.
[18] Net result: Parliament moves fast, but only if it can brand this as “national champion + strict oversight”, not a carve-up.
[20] 2) What Finance/Justice/Energy demand before they’ll let it proceed
[21] Even with Strevo offering transparency, the system will force structure, because the political cost of “ethics panic” is real.
[22] The required “clean-room” conditions
[23] Ownership clarity: Strevo’s 70% net worth injection can’t sit in a murky bucket. The clean solution the Finance Committee demands is:
[24] Strevo funds Horizon via non-voting preferred equity or convertible debt (publicly disclosed terms),
[25] while Curro (70%) and the King (30%) hold the voting common shares only if Curro places his stake in a blind trust / managed holding while he’s Finance Minister.
[26] Procurement firewall: Horizon cannot bid on state contracts unless:
[27] tenders are run under PPACRA rules,
[28] and an independent procurement panel signs off.
[29] Export control compliance: Parliament inserts language that all sensitive exports require Cabinet approval and must follow “Reunion strategic interest” rules.
[30] Security oversight: RNIA/Interior require:
[31] vetting of all foreign technical staff,
[32] and strict control of remote diagnostics and comms systems.
[33] Translation: Parliament won’t stop it, but it will chain it to oversight so it doesn’t become the country’s next corruption engine.
[35] 3) The bill that actually passes (early October)
[36] BILL No. 207/1992 — Horizon Dynamics National Consolidation & Mobilization Act (HDNCMA)
[37] Passed: 9 October 1992
 Sponsors: RCA + NSF + RRP modernization bloc (with LUP concessions)
 Key provisions:
[38] Authorizes mergers/buyouts of designated defense-industrial firms into Horizon Dynamics.
[39] Creates a Strategic Industrial Board (Finance + Energy + Defense + Justice + one parliamentary oversight seat) with veto power over:
[40] major acquisitions,
[41] related-party contracts,
[42] export destinations,
[43] and any “dual-use electronics” procurement.
[44] Requires public disclosure of capitalization structure, beneficial ownership, and annual audited accounts.
[45] Mandates local content and workforce training pipelines (HTESA tie-in).
[46] Vote sketch (typical outcome):
[47] RRP: strong majority for (with a chunk abstaining over conflicts)
[48] RCA/NSF: overwhelmingly for
[49] LUP: split (jobs wing votes yes; civil-liberties wing votes no/abstain)
[50] Dalmatian lists: mostly yes if logistics guarantees included
[52] 4) Who gets bought into Horizon (what survives)
[53] The Ministry of Energy & Industry’s consolidation list targets the “still-alive” shells:
[54] Lucania Motor Works (vehicle assembly + heavy diesel capability)
[55] Steinberg Ordnance & Foundry (metalwork, castings, barrels, industrial machining)
[56] Reunion Avionics & Instruments Group (electronics, radios, basic radar components)
[57] Torrental Heavy Logistics Works (trailers, cranes, port equipment)
[58] Reunion Systems Integration Bureau (small R&D office that becomes Horizon’s “brain”)
[59] Parliament insists a few civilian-leaning subsidiaries stay separately audited to prevent military slush funds from swallowing everything.
[61] 5) The four “big projects” — how the state reacts
[62] Project 1: Heavy logistics trucks (MAZ-537-like, plus smaller variant)
[63] Reception: best received of the four. Everyone understands trucks = logistics = survival.
 Defense and Infrastructure committees immediately earmark it as a priority because:
[64] it supports Dalmatia supply resilience,
[65] it supports rail/port reconstruction,
[66] it can export regionally later.
[67] Problem ministries flag: steel supply, engine supply chain, and QA discipline.
[68] Project 2: Radar competitive with a NATO market
[69] Reception: politically popular, technically hard.
 The military wants it; RRP wants “exportable industry”; but engineers warn:
[70] “competitive NATO radar” is not a 12–18 month win; it’s multi-year R&D + supply chain maturity.
[71] So Parliament frames it as:
[72] Phase 1: reliable coastal/ground surveillance radars for Reunion first
[73] Phase 2: export-grade systems later if credible
[74] Project 3: Broad electronics modernization capability
[75] Reception: universally supported if it stays dual-use.
 NDIDMA and HTESA give it cover: “modern chips, secure comms, industrial controls.”
 Justice Ministry demands strict compliance language so this doesn’t become an illegal procurement circus.
[76] Project 4: “Harpyiae” air-superiority fighter using MiG wreckage + a modern French jet purchase
[77] Reception: the most controversial.
[78] Defense hawks love the dream, but the professional military/technocrats call it what it is: expensive, slow, and politically risky.
[79] France will sell aircraft, but they’ll insist on end-use controls and will not bless a scheme that looks like cloning or tech diversion.
[80] RNIA and Justice are alarmed by anything resembling backdoor acquisition of controlled US components.
[81] So Parliament’s likely compromise:
[82] Approve purchase of a modern French air-superiority platform for immediate capability (e.g., Mirage 2000C/B era) under strict terms, and
[83] authorize a long-range domestic R&D program focused on avionics, materials, and flight testing—without pretending a clean-sheet air-superiority fighter appears quickly.
[85] 6) The corporate bidding/positioning you asked for
[86] Foreign majors (lobbying pressure)
[87] They don’t bid for “percentages of Horizon” directly at first; they bid for:
[88] joint ventures, supply contracts, engine lines, radar subassemblies, avionics modules, and tooling packages.
[89] Likely lobbying actors:
[90] Dassault / Thomson-CSF (France) around aircraft and radar
[91] US firms will be cautious and lawyer-heavy because of export control issues
[92] Domestic power plays
[93] Younger Industries: bids to become the prime domestic subcontractor (engines, heavy manufacturing, logistics fleet), and tries to lock in truck production as “civil + military.”
[94] Curro (small play): triggers immediate ethics scrutiny. Even if it’s clean, Parliament forces his stake to be insulated while he’s Finance Minister.
[95] King Zo / Royla: goes huge—wins influence through:
[96] capital injection,
[97] port logistics and security contracts,
[98] and board control pressure.
[99] Who “gets what” (politically plausible allocation)
[100] Curro’s 70% voting stake only survives if placed behind a compliance wall (managed holding/blind trust structure while in office).
[101] Royla’s 30% buys board seats and strategic control language, but Parliament blocks Royla from being the sole gatekeeper on exports or procurement awards.
[102] Strevo’s big money goes in as preferred capital with transparent terms, so Parliament can say: “He’s funding national industry, not buying a private army.”
[104] If you want, I can write the committee hearing summary (the objections, the amendments, the exact “ethics firewall” clauses), and a one-page Horizon corporate structure showing how Strevo’s massive investment fits without contradicting the Curro/Zo 70/30 ownership split.

sources.path: REUNION/July 1st, 1992 – “Reunion Broadcasting Daily” Morning Edition.docx
sources.text:
[1] July 1st, 1992 – “Reunion Broadcasting Daily” Morning Edition
[2] REUNION BROADCASTING DAILY
 July 1st, 1992
[4] Front Page
[5] PRESIDENT DONAHUE SIGNS FOUR KEY POSTWAR LAWS
 New Framework for Veterans, Reconstruction, Emergencies, and April 6th Accountability
[6] Reunion City – President Dax Donahue yesterday signed four major pieces of legislation into law, in what observers are calling the first coherent phase of the postwar settlement.
[7] The bills, passed by the Assembly between June 25th and July 1st, are:
[8] Evinos & Marine Pocket Veterans Relief Act
[9] Establishes disability pensions and medical support for wounded veterans of Evinos and the Marine Pocket, as well as stipends for widows and orphans.
[10] Creates a unified National Veterans Registry to standardize claims and prevent fraud.
[11] Post-War Reconstruction & Stabilization Fund Act
[12] Creates a 10-year Reconstruction Fund, initially capitalized at 250 million RMC.
[13] Prioritizes critical infrastructure on all three main islands, with early focus on ports, roads, and power in Reunion City and Torrental.
[14] Introduces a “soft” deficit ceiling, signaling intent to keep public finances under control.
[15] Emergency Powers & Martial Law Sunset Act
[16] Formally ends martial law in Reunion City and other affected areas on a fixed timetable unless renewed by a supermajority of the Assembly.
[17] Tightens rules around states of emergency, requiring shorter initial durations and more frequent parliamentary review.
[18] Limits extended pre-charge detention and mandates reporting on emergency operations.
[19] Families of April 6th Victims Compensation & Policing Review Act
[20] Provides compensation schemes for families of those killed on April 6th—police, soldiers, security staff, and civilians.
[21] Establishes an independent commission to review public-order policing tactics and recommend reforms to use-of-force protocols.
[22] In a brief signing statement, President Donahue described the package as “the beginning of a long process of repair—of our infrastructure, of our institutions, and of our conscience.”
[24] Second Lead
[25] PALACE, JUSTICE MINISTRY FLOAT ‘CONSTITUTIONAL HOUSEKEEPING’
[26] Reunion City – Legal and political circles are buzzing after it emerged that the Ministry of Justice, in coordination with palace legal advisers, has requested a cabinet discussion next week on what is being described as “technical modernization of constitutional language.”
[27] Sources in the Assembly say the discussion will focus on:
[28] Clarifying the Crown’s consultative role in matters of war, peace, constitutional amendments, and key appointments,
[29] Harmonizing emergency provisions with current practice,
[30] Codifying the balance of powers between the Presidency, the Assembly, and the monarchy.
[31] Officials emphasize there is “no question” of abolishing the presidency or overturning the republic. Supporters argue that outdated 1946 wording needs to be brought in line with the evolved role of the Crown as a “guardian of continuity.”
[32] Privately, some opposition figures worry that vague language about “moral guardianship” could, over time, give the palace more leverage over legislation and security policy than is currently acknowledged.
[33] A full cabinet session on the topic is expected in early July.
[35] Politics & Parties
[36] ROYALIST PARTY SIGNALS IDEOLOGICAL SHIFT AHEAD OF EXTRAORDINARY CONGRESS
[37] Reunion City – The Royalist Conservative Alliance (RCA) executive committee has approved draft changes to its program ahead of an extraordinary party congress planned for later this year.
[38] The new platform language:
[39] Places stronger emphasis on “national identity anchored in the Crown,”
[40] Calls for a harder line against terrorism, separatism, and foreign interference,
[41] Elevates traditional values, family, and faith as pillars of the state,
[42] Frames the monarchy as “the living symbol of Reunion’s unity and historical continuity.”
[43] Several senior RCA figures insist the party remains “firmly democratic,” but admit that the tone is shifting to capture disaffected nationalist and security-focused voters who have drifted toward the NSF in recent years.
[44] Observers in Parliament note that Royalist MPs have become more vocal in debates on internal security and culture, presenting themselves as the “serious patriotic alternative” between leftist populism and militarized hardliners.
[46] Economy & Society
[47] RECONSTRUCTION FUND RAISES HOPES AND QUESTIONS
[48] Reunion City – Business associations and trade unions cautiously welcomed the Post-War Reconstruction & Stabilization Fund, but questions remain about priorities and oversight.
[49] Finance Ministry estimates suggest the Fund, together with veterans’ programs, could reach around 1% of GDP per year in new spending during the first phase.
[50] Economists close to the government argue that:
[51] If directed toward high-impact projects (ports, rail, power),
[52] And paired with tighter control of wasteful legacy programs,
[53] the spending could boost long-term growth and employment.
[54] Skeptics warn that without strong anti-corruption safeguards, the Fund risks becoming “another sink for favors and political construction contracts.”
[55] A separate Public Procurement & Anti-Corruption Reform Act, strengthening transparency and oversight of government contracts, is reported to be advancing through committee and could reach the Assembly floor later in July.
[57] Security & Internal Affairs
[58] INTELLIGENCE OVERSIGHT BILL GAINS MOMENTUM
[59] Reunion City – The Interim Intelligence Oversight & Reporting Act, which would create a temporary parliamentary subcommittee to oversee RIA and GRI activities and demand a full inventory of their programs, has passed key committee stages and is expected to see a plenary vote in the coming weeks.
[60] The bill is widely seen as a precursor to a deeper reorganization of the intelligence community, including the proposed creation of a more clearly civilian Reunion National Intelligence Agency (RNIA).
[61] Government spokespeople present the move as “normalization after war,” while critics warn against weakening internal security as extremist cells and foreign influence operations continue to probe the country’s defenses.
[63] World & Foreign Desk
[64] MOSCOW STRAINS TO PROJECT POWER AFTER MEDITERRANEAN SETBACK
[65] Moscow – Soviet leadership is struggling to manage the fallout from recent naval losses in the Mediterranean, including the near-destruction of its operational submarine force in the theater.
[66] Official statements from Premier Somov Antonovich emphasize “strategic patience” and highlight economic recovery plans, but party insiders and foreign diplomats report:
[67] Intensifying internal debates between economic reformers and hardline security figures,
[68] Renewed emphasis on covert and proxy operations abroad, particularly in southern Europe and friendly regimes.
[69] While large-scale Soviet military action against Reunion is widely considered unlikely in the short term, intelligence sources in several Western capitals note increased activity by Soviet advisers and covert operatives in People’s Greece, the Balkans, and sympathetic movements across the Mediterranean.
[71] UNITED STATES CONSOLIDATES GULF POSITION, WATCHES MOSCOW AND ATHENS
[72] Washington – The United States continues to solidify its military foothold in the Persian Gulf after the defeat of Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait.
[73] Key developments:
[74] No-fly zones over Iraq remain in effect.
[75] US and allied naval forces maintain persistent patrols to secure shipping lanes.
[76] American analysts track Soviet moves closely, wary of any renewed Moscow–Baghdad or Moscow–Damascus arms channels.
[77] In southern Europe, US policy circles watch the Reunion–Soviet confrontation with mixed feelings: relief that Reunion has held its ground at sea, but concern that repeated crises could drag NATO into a larger confrontation.
[78] Unofficially, Washington views Reunion as a useful, if unpredictable, partner—valuable in checking Soviet influence, but risky if domestic instability or overreach triggers a wider escalation.
[80] BALKANS REMAIN UNSTABLE AS CROATIA CONSOLIDATES, BOSNIA FRACTURES
[81] Zagreb / Sarajevo – Croatia, having declared independence and fought multiple engagements against the collapsing Yugoslav federal structures, appears to be consolidating control over much of its claimed territory after a series of ceasefires.
[82] However:
[83] Bosnia is fracturing among rival factions with ethnic and ideological dimensions;
[84] Various “volunteer” formations, some with foreign backing, continue to move across porous borders.
[85] Regional analysts warn that Dalmatia under Reunion administration remains an exposed flank, with militant groups and criminal syndicates reportedly rearming and re-organizing in the shadows.
[87] PEOPLE’S GREECE: CIVIL CONFLICT GRINDS ON
[88] Athens / Thessaly – The communist government in People’s Greece continues to fight a draining conflict against insurgent formations such as the Hellenic Revival Movement.
[89] Recent weeks saw:
[90] Night raids, ambushes, and retaliatory operations in northern regions,
[91] Conflicting claims by state media and underground broadcasters over casualties and territory,
[92] Signs of Soviet advisers operating more openly in some sectors, according to Western intelligence assessments.
[93] No comprehensive settlement appears in sight; the conflict remains a slow bleed on both the Greek regime and its Soviet backers.
[95] Short Domestic Notes
[96] Rail Modernization Debate: The Transport Ministry is reportedly preparing a major proposal designating a Lucania–Steinberg–Reunion City–Torrental corridor as a strategic rail priority, with discussions of eventual electrification and faster passenger service. Branch lines would be upgraded to diesel in phases.
[97] Royal Ceremonies: The Palace has announced a sequence of remembrance events for Evinos and the Marine Pocket, as well as the April 6th victims. Several decorated officers and veterans’ representatives are expected to attend in prominent roles.
[98] Fuel Prices: A Temporary Fuel & Energy Price Stabilization bill is being discussed in committee amid growing public concern about rising household costs. Energy and Finance officials say they are “studying options” to cushion price shocks without permanently distorting markets.

sources.text:
[1] Odds the market snaps and you slide into recession
[2] Given your mix right now (active war pressure, brittle confidence, a big foreign loan with a lockbox, import dependence, uneven industry, shaky logistics, and Parliament publicly flailing), the odds are ugly.
[3] Define “market crash” in Reunion terms
[4] Not a Wall Street-style crash — you don’t have that kind of market depth. A “crash” for you looks like:
[5] a currency confidence event (RMC sells off, spreads widen, importers demand USD terms),
[6] a short-term credit freeze (contractors won’t extend terms; banks tighten lending),
[7] and/or runs/hoarding behavior (fuel, staples, hard currency).
[8] Probabilities (best realistic read)
[9] Next 30 days (through mid-October 1992):
[10] Market “crash” event: 80–90%
[11] Recession (GDP contraction): 95–100%
[12] Severe recession / “worse” (deep contraction + shortages/controls): 65–80%
[13] Next 6 months (through March 1993):
[14] Recession: 85–95%
[15] Severe recession: 70–85%
[16] Why the odds are so high
[17] War risk dominates pricing. If the ceasefire ends Sept 14 at 23:06 and fighting resumes, confidence breaks fast.
[18] The lockbox clause scares everyone. People hear “customs revenues are spoken for” and assume austerity or payment delays.
[19] Backwards/uneven industry + import dependence means any FX stress becomes real shortages quickly.
[20] Parliamentary paralysis is a multiplier: markets can tolerate bad news; they can’t tolerate “nobody is steering.”
[21] What lowers the crash odds fast
[22] A credible budget freeze/triage within 48 hours (not slogans).
[23] A public statement from Curro + Central Bank guaranteeing liquidity and explaining tranches plainly.
[24] Visible anti-hoarding actions without looking like martial law economics (targeted distribution, not blanket crackdowns).
[25] A clear plan for the ceasefire end (either extension track or defensive posture + logistics plan). Markets hate uncertainty more than bad outcomes.
[27] Budget meeting scheduled (in-canon, earliest realistic)
[28] Emergency Budget & Stabilization Conference
 Time: September 13, 1992 — 09:30 (first workable hour after sunrise)
 Location: Presidential Palace, Reunion City — Secure Cabinet Room
 Chair: President Donahue
 Lead presenter: Finance Minister Curro
[29] Mandatory attendees
[30] Central Bank Governor (with reserves/FX liquidity brief)
[31] Defense, Interior, Energy/Industry, Transport ministers
[32] Head of National Infrastructure Coordination Council
[33] Assembly Finance Committee Chair + Ranking Member (RRP)
[34] One whip from each bloc (RCA, LUP, NSF) under restricted rules
[35] RNIA liaison (counterintelligence risk, port/currency rumor tracking)
[36] Agenda (90 minutes, hard clock)
[37] Cash position & reserves (what can be paid, what can’t)
[38] Tranche plan (first 30 days spending list, itemized)
[39] Lockbox implications (what revenue gets routed, what is protected)
[40] War sustainment minimum (fuel, spares, medical, comms)
[41] Inflation/hoarding response (food/fuel stabilization logistics)
[42] Contractor payment policy (stop the “panic invoices” spiral)
[43] Public messaging (one statement, one narrative)
[44] Output required by 12:00
[45] A one-page Emergency Budget Directive: freezes, protected categories, and a 30-day procurement list.
